options_ranked.title: Base Oil Procurement Audit, Forward Hedging, and Supplier Consolidation
options_ranked.description: Execute an urgent procurement diagnostic quantifying YTD base-oil cost-per-unit inflation versus prior year for Synthetic Blend and Conventional formulations — explicitly distinguishing a real input-cost shock from an overhead-allocation or costing-methodology artifact. Then lock input costs via a 90-day forward hedge (futures, supplier contracts, or inventory-timing) and consolidate fragmented supplier orders for negotiating leverage. Scope: targets the shared cost driver behind Engine Oils (-5.80 pp line-level), Compressor Oil (-5.86 pp) and Hydraulic Oil (-5.76 pp); no commercial or contract exposure, so anchor-account constraints are untouched.
options_ranked.rationale: The synchronized erosion across all oil grades (-7.14, -6.61, -5.86, -5.76 pp) is the signature of a common upstream cost shock, and base oil is a client-confirmed COGS component — the most defensible causal ground of the three options. Crucially, the diagnostic step also tests whether any portion of the drop is a measurement artifact before capital is committed to hedges, and the mechanism requires no customer-facing action, so it cannot breach the price-lock constraint.
options_ranked.time_to_value: 60-90 days (audit results in 2-3 weeks; hedge effect lags 1-2 months)

arguments_for: Attacks the confirmed COGS pathway directly, protecting margin across the entire affected portfolio, not just one SKU family.
The audit step guards against spending against a phantom problem if part of the variance turns out to be an allocation artifact.
arguments_against: Hedging locks in current elevated prices — if base oil costs fall, the business forgoes the recovery and carries hedge cost.
This defends against further erosion more reliably than it claws back the pp already lost; full recovery depends on where the forward curve sits versus prior-year cost.
key_questions: What is the exact YTD base oil cost-per-unit delta versus prior year, and what does the forward curve imply for the next two quarters?
What hedge instruments and counterparty limits are already available to treasury?

implementation_triggers: Procurement audit confirms base oil unit-cost inflation explains the majority of the COGS increase.
Forward curve pricing sits at or below current spot, making a 90-day lock economically favorable.
prerequisites: COGS decomposition by account category (raw materials, manufacturing, distribution, packaging — all confirmed COGS components) to isolate the base-oil contribution and rule out allocation artifacts.
Treasury sign-off on hedge instruments, counterparty exposure, and notional limits.
Supplier spend map identifying consolidation candidates.

impact_estimate.basis: Stabilizing base oil input cost recovers 50–80% of the -7.14 pp Synthetic Blend and -6.61 pp Conventional declines via the confirmed base_oil_cost→COGS→Gross Margin % pathway, assuming partial hedge execution and a 1–2 month lag; this sizes the affected engine-oil segment, not the enterprise headline.

key_assumptions.assumption: Base oil cost inflation, not volume, discounting, or a costing artifact, is the dominant driver of the synchronized margin decline.
key_assumptions.provenance: Inferred from the cross-grade pattern; confirmed if the procurement audit shows base oil cost-per-unit up materially YoY while price and volume per unit are broadly flat — falsified if unit costs are flat and the variance sits in allocation.

key_assumptions.assumption: Base oil is a confirmed component of COGS that flows directly into Gross Margin %.
key_assumptions.provenance: Client-confirmed causal edges: base_oil_cost → COGS (account_category component) and COGS ↔ gross_margin_pct.

key_assumptions.assumption: Forward hedging can be executed at pricing that stabilizes or reduces effective input cost over the next 90 days.
key_assumptions.provenance: Falsified if the forward curve trades persistently above current spot, making the lock value-destructive.

options_ranked.title: Selective Price Indexation on Premium Synthetic Blend Tiers with Mix Incentive Rebalancing
options_ranked.description: Within the anchor-account price-lock constraint, implement tiered price recovery on Synthetic Blend premium variants (High Mileage, Extended Drain) for non-anchor and renewal-cycle accounts only, after a contract screen confirms which SKUs and accounts fall outside the lock. In parallel, restructure distributor and retail incentives to shift volume away from Value-tier SKUs (which fell -6.42 pp to 19.82%) toward higher-margin grades. Scope: targets Synthetic Blend and Value-tier economics — no intervention needed on timeframe buckets already within threshold, and anchor accounts are explicitly excluded until renewal windows open.
options_ranked.rationale: Price/volume/mix decomposition points at revenue-side recovery as the fastest lever available while the input-cost driver persists. Because blanket repricing is contractually blocked mid-quarter, the mechanism is deliberately narrowed to non-locked accounts and premium tiers where willingness-to-pay is highest. The mix-uplift portion is deliberately sized conservatively because the premium-mix-to-margin relationship is an unconfirmed industry prior, not a validated driver in this dataset — the priced portion of the recovery does not depend on it.

arguments_for: Directly recovers margin on the single largest driver of the decline (Synthetic Blend, -7.14 pp) without waiting for commodity markets to normalize.
Incentive rebalancing is self-funding if rebate dollars are reallocated rather than added, keeping cost near-neutral.
arguments_against: If a large share of Synthetic Blend volume sits inside anchor-account locks, the addressable base shrinks and recovery falls toward the low end.
Price increases in a cost-inflation environment risk volume leakage to competitors, which would compress net revenue and offset the margin gain.
key_questions: What exact percentage of Synthetic Blend revenue is contractually price-locked this quarter?
What price elasticity have non-anchor accounts shown in prior indexation cycles?

implementation_triggers: Contract screen confirms ≥35% of Synthetic Blend volume is outside price-locked agreements.
Procurement audit confirms input-cost inflation (not a costing artifact) as the driver, justifying price recovery messaging to customers.
prerequisites: SKU-by-account contract screen to identify which Synthetic Blend SKUs fall under anchor price locks — mandatory before any indexation to avoid breaching the mid-quarter constraint.
Customer-level margin and willingness-to-pay segmentation of the non-anchor book.
Redesign of distributor incentive tiers with finance sign-off on rebate economics.

impact_estimate.basis: Selective indexation on the estimated 40–50% of Synthetic Blend volume outside the anchor price lock recovers ~2.5–3.5 pp against that product's -7.14 pp decline, plus 1.0–1.7 pp from mix rebalancing away from the Value tier's -6.42 pp drag; this sizes the Synthetic Blend segment, not the enterprise headline.

key_assumptions.assumption: At least 40% of Synthetic Blend volume is outside anchor-account price locks and addressable this quarter.
key_assumptions.provenance: Contract screen output showing the price-locked share of Synthetic Blend revenue below 60%.

key_assumptions.assumption: Shifting mix toward premium grades lifts blended Gross Margin %.
key_assumptions.provenance: Rests on an unconfirmed industry prior (premium mix ↔ margin); falsified if current SKU-level margin data shows premium grades no longer carry a margin advantage after input-cost inflation.

key_assumptions.assumption: Non-anchor accounts will absorb an 8–12% price index with limited volume loss.
key_assumptions.provenance: Post-implementation volume tracking: volume decline in indexed accounts stays under 5% for two consecutive months.

flagged_side_effects: The mix-uplift portion of this option leans on an unconfirmed relationship between premium mix and blended margin, and indexing premium Synthetic Blend SKUs could inadvertently touch price-locked anchor contracts. Addressed by making the SKU-by-account contract screen a hard prerequisite and by sizing the priced recovery independently of the mix assumption.

options_ranked.title: Portfolio Reallocation: De-emphasize Structurally Impaired Value-Tier Grades, Redirect to Margin-Accretive Formulations
options_ranked.description: Reframe the question from 'how do we fix these product margins' to 'do these products belong in the portfolio at current cost structures.' Over 3–12 months, reduce sales-mix exposure to Value-tier Conventional and Synthetic Blend grades and selectively exit SKUs where input-cost inflation has eroded structural profitability, redirecting volume to formulations that hold a verified margin advantage. CONSISTENCY NOTE: the data shows margin compression across ALL measured grades (Compressor Oil -5.86 pp, Hydraulic Oil -5.76 pp), so no target segment is yet confirmed as margin-advantaged — Step 1 is therefore a current-margin verification of candidate target formulations (e.g., Full Synthetic, specialty), and reallocation proceeds only toward grades with a demonstrated ≥5 pp margin premium at today's costs.
options_ranked.rationale: If input-cost inflation is structural rather than cyclical, price and hedging levers only delay the reckoning; composition change is the durable fix. The critic concern that de-emphasizing volume could reduce net revenue through the confirmed units-sold→revenue pathway is addressed by making margin verification of target formulations and a volume-absorption plan hard prerequisites — no volume is shed before its destination is confirmed accretive.

arguments_for: Delivers a durable margin structure that does not depend on commodity prices reverting or on customers accepting price increases.
Exit economics on structurally impaired SKUs free working capital and manufacturing capacity for higher-return formulations.
arguments_against: Every measured grade in the data shows margin compression, so the assumed margin-accretive destination for reallocated volume is not yet evidenced — if premium grades are equally compressed, the composition gain evaporates.

De-emphasizing Value-tier volume that is not fully absorbed elsewhere reduces net revenue (units sold drives revenue by confirmed definition) and risks ceding shelf space and customer relationships that are hard to recover.
key_questions: What are the current, post-inflation gross margins of Full Synthetic and specialty formulations, and do they exceed Value-tier grades by at least 5 pp?
What share of de-emphasized Value-tier volume can realistically be converted rather than lost?

implementation_triggers: Procurement audit indicates base oil inflation is structural (persisting beyond two quarters) rather than a cyclical spike.
Margin verification confirms target formulations hold ≥5 pp margin premium at current input costs.
prerequisites: SKU-level current-margin verification of all candidate target formulations before any volume is shifted (resolves the risk of reallocating toward equally compressed segments).
Volume-absorption and customer-migration plan quantifying expected net revenue retention.
Exit-economics model per candidate SKU (contribution margin, capacity release, customer contract obligations).

impact_estimate.basis: If reallocation halves the blended-margin contribution of Synthetic Blend (-7.14 pp) and Conventional (-6.61 pp) and redirects that volume to formulations verified to carry 5–7 pp higher margin at current costs, portfolio Gross Margin % recovers 3.5–5.8 pp at enterprise level; the high end exceeds the -4.49 pp enterprise headline decline and would only be reached if reallocation also lifts margin above the prior baseline.

key_assumptions.assumption: Higher-margin formulations exist in the portfolio and retain a ≥5 pp margin advantage at current input costs.
key_assumptions.provenance: SKU-level margin report at current costs; falsified if premium formulations show compression comparable to the -5.8 to -7.1 pp seen across measured grades.

key_assumptions.assumption: A premium-mix shift lifts blended Gross Margin %.
key_assumptions.provenance: Rests on an unconfirmed industry-template prior; must be validated with actual SKU margin data before reallocation begins.

key_assumptions.assumption: At least half of de-emphasized Value-tier volume can be converted to target formulations rather than lost.
key_assumptions.provenance: Falsified if pilot-account migration shows conversion below 40%, in which case net revenue loss via the confirmed units-sold→revenue link outweighs the composition gain.

key_assumptions.assumption: The input-cost pressure is structural, not a cyclical spike that will revert within 2-3 quarters.
key_assumptions.provenance: Base oil cost remaining elevated versus prior-year benchmark for two additional consecutive quarters would be consistent with structural pressure.

flagged_side_effects: De-emphasizing Value-tier and Synthetic Blend volume risks reducing net revenue through the confirmed units-sold→revenue relationship if reallocated volume is not fully absorbed by target formulations, and the assumed mix-to-margin benefit is an unconfirmed prior. Mitigated by hard prerequisites: verify target-formulation margins at current costs and model volume absorption before any de-emphasis begins.

solutions.recommendation_rationale: The synchronized margin erosion across Synthetic Blend (-7.14 pp), Conventional (-6.61 pp), Compressor Oil (-5.86 pp) and Hydraulic Oil (-5.76 pp) is the signature of a shared input-cost driver, and base oil is the only candidate confirmed by the client as a direct COGS component flowing into Gross Margin %. The procurement audit and hedge attacks that confirmed pathway without any customer-facing action, so it cannot breach the anchor-account price-lock, and its diagnostic step also determines whether the pricing and portfolio plays are worth pursuing — the audit output is the gating evidence for both. The pricing play should launch in parallel once the contract screen confirms the addressable non-anchor base.

problem_reframe.situation: Enterprise Gross Margin % has dropped year-to-date to 29.94% from 34.43% (-4.49 pp, -13.0%), with the sharpest compression concentrated in Synthetic Blend Engine Oil (-7.14 pp to 20.64%) and Conventional Engine Oil (-6.61 pp to 19.16%).
problem_reframe.complication: The erosion is synchronized across nearly all oil grades — Synthetic Blend (-7.14 pp), Conventional (-6.61 pp), Compressor Oil (-5.86 pp), Hydraulic Oil (-5.76 pp) and the Value category (-6.42 pp) — a pattern consistent with a shared input-cost driver (base oil is a confirmed COGS component) rather than SKU-specific demand loss. Meanwhile a contractual price-lock prevents mid-quarter list-price increases on Lubricants anchor accounts, closing off the most direct commercial response, and no timeframe bucket shows offsetting strength that can be simply scaled.
problem_reframe.question: Which combination of cost-side, price/mix, and portfolio levers can recover 3.5+ percentage points of Gross Margin % without breaching anchor-account price locks or sacrificing net revenue?
key_assumptions: The margin decline is real economics, not a costing-methodology or allocation artifact (to be verified in the procurement audit).
Base oil cost inflation is the common driver behind synchronized multi-grade margin compression (inferred from pattern; confirmed only as a COGS component, not yet as the YTD cause).
Anchor-account price-lock clauses remain binding through the current quarter.
Higher-margin formulations exist in the portfolio and retain their historical margin advantage despite the same input-cost pressure.

unresolved_tensions.tension: Whether the input-cost pressure is cyclical (favoring hedging and selective repricing) or structural (favoring portfolio reallocation) cannot be resolved from YTD data alone.
unresolved_tensions.requires: Head of Procurement to deliver the base-oil cost audit with a 2-quarter forward-curve read to the CFO by end of Week 3, classifying the inflation as cyclical or structural.

unresolved_tensions.tension: Both the pricing play and the reallocation play depend on premium formulations actually carrying a margin advantage at current costs, but every grade measured in the data shows compression — the assumed margin-accretive destination is unverified.
unresolved_tensions.requires: Finance team to complete SKU-level current-cost margin verification of Full Synthetic and specialty formulations before any mix incentive or reallocation decision (target: Week 2).

unresolved_tensions.tension: The share of Synthetic Blend volume addressable for price indexation is unknown until anchor-account contract coverage is mapped, and the answer determines whether the pricing play clears its low-end recovery estimate.
unresolved_tensions.requires: Head of Commercial Operations to complete the SKU-by-account contract screen identifying price-locked versus addressable Synthetic Blend volume by end of Week 2.

blind_spots: No customer- or channel-dimension change points were surfaced, so concentrated discounting or a single large account's terms could be contributing without being visible in the product-level cuts.

The headline enterprise decline (-4.49 pp) is smaller than the product-level deltas (-5.8 to -7.1 pp), implying an offsetting segment or mix effect that has not been identified — understanding what is cushioning the blend could reveal a replication opportunity.

Distribution, packaging, and manufacturing costs are all confirmed COGS components; the council's hypotheses concentrate on base oil, and freight or packaging inflation could account for part of the compression.
Competitor pricing behavior is unobserved — if competitors are passing through the same input inflation, the price elasticity risk in the indexation play is materially lower than assumed.

proposed_option.title: Targeted SKU-Level Price Indexation on Synthetic Blend Premium Tiers + Mix Incentive Rebalancing
proposed_option.description: Within the contractual price-lock constraint on anchor accounts, implement a tiered price recovery on Synthetic Blend formulations (e.g., High Mileage, Extended Drain variants) targeting non-anchor or renewal-cycle accounts. Price-lock constraints prevent blanket repricing, but selective indexation on Synthetic Blend premium SKUs (which carry structurally higher margins) can recover margin dollars without breaching anchor account terms. Simultaneously, incentive rebalancing redirects volume from Value-tier (lower-margin) SKUs to premium Synthetic Blend, improving blended mix and offsetting commodity cost pressure through volume composition rather than pure price.

Selective price indexation targeting 8–12% uplift on premium SKUs (assuming 40–50% of Synthetic Blend volume qualifies outside anchor lock) recovers ~2.5–3.5 pp. Mix rebalancing toward Synthetic Blend from Value tier (6.42 pp decline) can capture 1.0–1.7 pp through volume shift, totaling 3.5–5.2 pp gross margin % recovery.

Hedging locks input cost, protecting margin until contract renewal or commercial renegotiation windows open post-Q2.
